{{short description|Indian scientist (born 1956)}}
{{EngvarB|date=February 2018}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2018}}
'''Gaiti Hasan''' (born November 1956) is an Indian scientist who researches in the fields of [[Drosophila melanogaster|Drosophila]] [[genetics]], [[neuroscience]] and [[Calcium signaling|intra cellular calcium signalling]].<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow">{{cite web|url=http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316225356/http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-date=16 March 2014 |title=Gaiti Hasan – INSA Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy www.insaindia.org |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref> She is expert in [[Reverse genetics]]. Hasan is a Fellow of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), the apex body of Indian scientists and technologists.<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow"/> From 2013 onwards she has been serving as a Senior Professor at the National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS), Bangalore.<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow">{{cite web|url=http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316225356/http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-date=16 March 2014 |title=Gaiti Hasan – INSA Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy www.insaindia.org |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref><ref name="NCBS Faculty">{{cite web | url=https://www.ncbs.res.in/node/152 | title=NCBS Faculty | publisher=National Centre for Biological Sciences www.ncbs.res.in | access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref> 

==Education==
Hasan studied in [[Aligarh]] as a child. Her parents taught at university, and her two sisters studied chemistry and physics.<ref name="Lilavati's Daughters - Gaiti Hasan">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/womeninscience/LD_essays/128-131.pdf | title=Science and the Art of Detection | work=Lilavati's Daughters: The Women Scientists of India | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |year=2008 | access-date=19 October 2014 | editor1= Godbole, Rohini |editor2=Ramaswamy, Ram | pages=128–131}}</ref> She went on to do a BSc in [[zoology]] from [[Miranda House]], [[Delhi University]] in 1976. She completed a MSc in [[life sciences]] in 1978 and a [[M.Phil.]] in 1980 from [[Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi|Jawaharlal Nehru University]], Delhi.<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow">{{cite web|url=http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316225356/http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-date=16 March 2014 |title=Gaiti Hasan – INSA Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy www.insaindia.org |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref><ref name="Lilavati's Daughters - Gaiti Hasan" /> In 1983, she received a PhD from the [[University of Cambridge]] for her dissertation on ribosomal RNA genes of [[Trypanosoma brucei]].<ref name="NISER Gaiti Hasan bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.niser.ac.in/~cellbio2011/speaker_profiles/Prof%20G%20Hasan.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227094315/http://www.niser.ac.in/~cellbio2011/speaker_profiles/Prof%20G%20Hasan.pdf |archive-date=27 February 2018 |title=NISER Gaiti Hasan bio |publisher=National Institute of Science Education and Research www.niser.ac.in |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref> According to Hasan, it was while she was applying to universities for her PhD that she realised for the first time that "belonging to a minority could lead to discrimination". She believes this has led her to "consciously try and be supportive of other woman scientists, be they students or colleagues".<ref name="Lilavati's Daughters - Gaiti Hasan" />

==Career==
Presently she works at NCBS ([[National Centre for Biological Sciences]])<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncbs.res.in/faculty/gaiti|title=NCBS Faculty|website=ncbs.res.in|access-date=16 July 2016}}</ref> where she researches on the systemic and cellular consequences of changes in intracellular calcium levels in animals. In 1983, Hasan joined the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) in [[Mumbai]], as a visiting fellow and research associate in the molecular biology unit.<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow">{{cite web|url=http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316225356/http://www.insaindia.org/detail.php?id=P06-1411 |archive-date=16 March 2014 |title=Gaiti Hasan – INSA Fellow |publisher=Indian National Science Academy www.insaindia.org |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref> She was a visiting scientist at the biology department in [[Brandeis University]] [[Massachusetts]] in 1992.<ref name="NISER Gaiti Hasan bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.niser.ac.in/~cellbio2011/speaker_profiles/Prof%20G%20Hasan.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227094315/http://www.niser.ac.in/~cellbio2011/speaker_profiles/Prof%20G%20Hasan.pdf |archive-date=27 February 2018 |title=NISER Gaiti Hasan bio |publisher=National Institute of Science Education and Research www.niser.ac.in |access-date=19 October 2014 }}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Hasan has received a scholarship from the Inlaks Foundation,<ref name="Hasan - Inlaks">{{cite web | url=http://inlaksfoundation.org/Alumni.aspx?sort=old&Type=A&SortAlpha=G | title=Inlaks Shivdasani Scholarships – Gaiti Hasan | publisher=Inlaks Shivdasani Foundation | access-date=14 April 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403154948/http://www.inlaksfoundation.org/Alumni.aspx?sort=old&Type=A&SortAlpha=G | archive-date=3 April 2015 }}</ref> a British Overseas Research Student Award, a fellowship from the [[Wellcome Trust]] and a [[Rockefeller Fellowship|Rockefeller]] Biotechnology Career Fellowship. In 2006, she was elected a Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], Bangalore and in 2007, as a Member of the [[Asia-Pacific Molecular Biology Network]].<ref name="Gaiti Hasan - INSA Fellow"/> She is also a fellow of [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA). In 2019, she received '''Sir M. Visvesvaraya Lifetime Achievement Award''' for senior scientists and engineers from Government of Karnataka, India.
